description: Run a Go module's wired static-analysis and style checks — golangci-lint v2 (`golangci-lint run --output.json.path …`, a `version: "2"` config with `linters` and `formatters` sections; issues bucketed as `<linter>` or `<linter>:<rule>` — `revive:exported`, `gosec:G204`, `staticcheck:SA1019`, `govet:printf`, `errcheck`, `unused` — and the `gofmt`/`goimports`/`gofumpt`/`gci` formatters as their own rule ids), `go vet -json` (analyzer names, `govet:<analyzer>`), `gofmt -l` when golangci-lint isn't wired, and govulncheck (`-format json`, `govulncheck:<GO-ID>`, split into called / imported-only / required-only) when installed — in any Go project (command-line tool, library, service), modules and `go.work` workspaces alike. Verifies each tool is installed and configured before trusting a "zero issues" result, reports an unwired tool as "not configured, skipped" rather than a clean pass, rejects a v1 golangci-lint config as a tooling failure (with the `golangci-lint migrate` fix) instead of silently linting with defaults, and parses every report with one embedded stdlib Python parser into per-tool totals and per-rule-id counts with a `file:line — message` list. Invoke as `/iru-go-code-quality` to check the whole module, or `/iru-go-code-quality <file-or-dir>[,<file-or-dir>...]` to scope the report (golangci-lint runs on the containing packages, since Go type-checks whole packages, and findings outside the scope are filtered out; govulncheck is always module-wide). When the prompt supplies a `baseline:` (a prior per-tool/per-rule-id count or itemized list from an earlier run of this skill, e.g. captured by `iru-go-code-one-task-group` before a task group's changes), reports only the new-vs-baseline diff per rule id. Report-only: never runs `golangci-lint run --fix`, `golangci-lint fmt` without `--diff`, `gofmt -w`, `goimports -w`, or `go mod tidy`, and never edits `.golangci.yml`. Use whenever the user wants a Go lint/vet/vulnerability pass called out separately from `iru-go-test`/`iru-go-coverage`, instead of eyeballing golangci-lint console output.
